name: VA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Bobby Scott running for re-election
Republican challenger raised only ~$6,600, no outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Bobby Scott holds a heavily Democratic district with incumbency advantages, while his Republican opponent has raised almost nothing and no outside groups are engaged. Markets and fundamentals both point to an overwhelming Democratic win, so the forecast stays at a wide margin.
model.watch: Any surprise outside spending or a polling shock would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bobby Scott, a longtime Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election in a southeastern Virginia district that leans Democratic by about 18 points. He has renominated without difficulty and holds a large financial edge, with roughly $688,000 raised and $192,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Edwin Rivera, has raised about $6,600 and reports minimal cash, and no outside spending has appeared on either side. Two independent candidates are on the ballot but show little financial activity.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the race rests on fundamentals: the district's strong Democratic lean, Scott's incumbency, and the lopsided fundraising gap. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. All available evidence points to a safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
